To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the initial-link schedule maintained by the two-component chained and by the tandem schedules was not sensitive to the presence of component-correlated stimuli, to the relative durations of these stimuli, or to the presence of a stimulus change that occurred when the component-correlated stimulus was present.

the terminal-link schedule arrangement has no effect on initial-link responding and that initial-link responses are not distributed equally on the initial keys when the initial and terminal links are associated with different interreinforcement interval sets.

the terminal-link schedule arrangement affects initial-link responding only when the terminal-link schedules are differentially signalled and that the initial-link schedule affects terminal-link responding only when it is differentially signalled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of differential stimulus control on the acquisition and performance of chained schedules.
the role that conditioned reinforcement plays in maintaining behavior.
the effects of differential stimulus control on choice between two concurrently available schedules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
conditioned reinforcement is a real phenomenon that has been misinterpreted in the context of chained schedules.

the present results are not inconsistent with the hypothesis that initial-link responding in this situation is maintained by the delayed primary reinforcement, but they are not conclusive in favor of this interpretation.

the results of the present experiments support the hypothesis that terminal-link components serve a discriminative function in a two-component chained schedule, but that the same components do not serve a conditioned reinforcement function in the initial link of a two-component schedule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of the component stimuli on initial-link performance are not mediated by conditioned reinforcement, but by the stimuli's ability to signal the availability of the terminal-link schedule.

, when a schedule of reinforcement is composed of two or more components arranged in series, each component is a discriminative stimulus for the next, and the terminal component is a discriminant for the reinforcer.
the two-component tandem and chained schedules are not equivalent in the sense that they produce the same pattern of terminal-link responding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence and relative durations of different component-correlated stimuli do not affect responding during the initial links.
we should be careful to avoid the assumption that a stimulus that is correlated with reinforcement must function as a conditioned reinforcer.

the presence and duration of component-correlated stimuli in a two-component chained schedule do not influence initial-link responding, and that this result suggests that initial-link responding might be maintained by delayed primary reinforcement rather than conditioned reinforcement.
